messages:
maggie: Heads-up — I'm going to run a short synthetic-heartbeat canary across streaming and embedding endpoints in ap-southeast1 at 10:15 UTC. It'll ramp to ~200 rps for 15m then backoff. Expect slightly higher token volume and a couple of transient 5xx while warm caches.
kai: noted. what's the sampling & backoff plan? we don't want noisy alerts.
maggie: plan is: 30s interval per target, ramp 1x -> 5x -> 1x over 15m, with jitter. If streaming handshake latency > 600ms for 3/5 samples, mark endpoint degraded. For embeddings: p95 latency > 350ms for 3/5 samples. We'll mute noisy alerts and post an incident if degraded persists >10m.
ben: can you paste the prometheus expression you plan to use for the streaming handshake check?\
maggie: sure — using blackbox-style metric we export: ``probe_success{job="heartbeat-stream"}`` and a derived latency: ``histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(probe_duration_seconds_bucket{job="heartbeat-stream"}[5m])) by (le))``. Grafana panel at https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streaming-heartbeats
priya: for ap-southeast1 we're already at 78% GPU pool utilization during peak. ramping tests could hit autoscaler thresholds — do we want to pin this to dedicated fallback nodes?
samir: +1 on fallback. Suggest we route the canary to a small shadow pool (dedicated:canary-1) to avoid triggering large scale-ups. If fallback not available, throttle ramp to 80 rps.
maggie: good idea. I'll route via canary-1. Config snippet I'm going to apply to the canary runner:
```
canary:
  targets:
    - stream://ap-southeast1/stream-ep
    - embed://ap-southeast1/embed-ep
  qps: 200
  ramp: [1,5,1]
  window: 15m
  backoff: {on_fail: exponential, jitter: true}
  routing: {pool: dedicated:canary-1, preserve_kv_cache: false}
```
monitor-bot: Alert suppression: silenced alert group "SRE/heartbeat-flapping" for 20m (reason: scheduled canary).
kai: thanks — can you also add a temporary tweak to the alert rule? Change streaming-handshake alert to fire at 5m sustained instead of 3m for this window.
maggie: done, rule patched. Link: https://prometheus.redwood.example/alerts/rules/streaming-handshake
ben: what about cost tracking? embedding token egress + probe frequency could add up if we repeat across regions. Do we log probe token usage separately?
maggie: yes — probe-runner emits probe_token_count and probe_estimated_cost_usd. I'll aggregate per region and post a one-off cost line in the runbook. Expect ~USD 8 for this run (embeddings heavy).
priya: keep an eye on SNAT port exhaustion in that region. Last time we ran a heavy canary we hit ephemeral port limits on the NAT gateway and endpoints started failing with ECONNRESET.
samir: if NAT looks tight we can spin a temporary egress-ngw (2x) for the canary window. Ops automation can create & wire it in ~6m.
maggie: will do. I'll also capture logs from the sidecar for any streaming handshake failures: snippet of what I'll grep:
```
# look for websocket errors and tls timings
kubectl logs -l app=stream-sidecar -n ap-southeast1 | egrep "Handshake|ECONNRESET|timeout" -A3
```
monitor-bot: canary-runner: job started (id=cny-1934567890), targets=2, expected_duration=15m
ben: quick thought — consider sampling embeddings requests with smaller context for probes (shorter sequences) so token costs drop but we still exercise model graph. Might change latency characteristics though.
maggie: agreed — for embeddings probe I'll swap to 64-token batched payloads for canary. Streaming needs to exercise longer-lived websocket handshake so keep as-is.
kai: after canary, let's run a short traffic shadow at 10% of normal for 30m to validate KV cache warmup behaviour under real load.
maggie: note taken. Post-run checklist: publish probe metrics, revert alert rule patch, delete canary pool, upload logs + cost summary to #eng-sre-runbooks. Will ping when complete. :thumbsup:
monitor-bot: canary-runner: job completed (id=cny-1934567890), result=partial_failures(2/120 samples), avg_stream_latency=420ms, avg_embed_latency=310ms, est_cost_usd=7.84"
